body:
### Zen 4 numbers for this PR, beside #584 (Threadripper 7980X)

The PR's table has no Zen 3 or Zen 4 data, so here is a CPU-only bench on a Threadripper 7980X (Zen 4, AVX-512, fast `pdep`). The trees:
- v1.1.35;
- #584 (414329b);
- this PR (b772203);
- the two merged.

All trees were built with `-march=native`. The bench uses **real expert weights** from a DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash IQ2_XXS (GSQ-RCO) pack: 64 experts a format pair, calls rotating through them.
- **Coverage:** all 8 gate-up / down format pairs of the pack, nt = 1 / 2 / 4 tokens a call (decode, and what an expert gets inside a verify window), threads 1 / 8 / 16 / 22 / 32.
- **Timing:** each point is the median of 60 calls; the table gives the median of 5 interleaved rounds. Run-to-run spread is 1 % (median), 3 % (90th percentile).

**Exact in every tree:**
- `native_rows_exact_test` gives "all identical", also with `DS4_IQ1M_PDEP=0` and `=1`.
- `ds4_iq1_rows_test`: 36 cases, 0 differ from ggml-cpu's dot.
- `ds4_lane_bench --check`: IQ1_M / IQ2_XS / IQ2_XXS own rows bit-identical to ggml's dot, at one token and at several.
- On the real experts, every format pair matches the double reference with the same errors in all four trees, and the start gate accepted every kernel.

**µs per expert, 22 threads, one expert a call:**

| gate-up / down (layers of 40 in this pack) | nt | v1.1.35 | #584 | this PR | both |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IQ1_M / IQ1_M (14) | 1 | 219 | 112 | 114 | 112 |
| | 2 | 248 | 250 | **166** | 168 |
| | 4 | 365 | 369 | **269** | 274 |
| IQ2_XXS / IQ1_M (9) | 1 | 151 | 119 | 120 | 119 |
| | 2 | 194 | 194 | **168** | 169 |
| IQ2_XS / IQ1_M (5) | 1 | 144 | 111 | **104** | 104 |
| | 2 | 210 | 210 | **183** | 185 |
| IQ1_M / IQ2_XXS (2) | 2 | 224 | 224 | **168** | 168 |
| IQ2_XS / IQ2_XS (1) | 1 | 112 | 112 | **100** | 100 |
| **weighted by layers** | 1 | 168 | 115 (1.46x) | 114 (1.46x) | 114 |
| | 2 | 212 | 213 (1.00x) | **171 (1.24x)** | 173 |
| | 4 | 297 | 299 (0.99x) | **249 (1.19x)** | 252 |

**Weighted by layers at the other thread counts** (v1.1.35 → this PR, nt 1 / 2 / 4):
- 1 thread: 1.57x / 1.29x / 1.23x;
- 8 threads: 1.52x / 1.28x / 1.22x;
- 32 threads: 1.44x / 1.22x / 1.18x.

With 3 experts a call at nt = 1 (22 threads), it is 140 → 95 µs in #584, this PR and both.

**What it says on Zen 4:**
- This PR alone has the whole gain: about 1.46x at one token, and 1.19-1.24x on the 2-4-token calls of verify windows. #584 leaves those calls alone. IQ2_XS one-token rows add 7-21 % on top.
- For IQ1_M at one token, ggml's BMI2 dot (#584's routing) is 1.5-3.5 % ahead of this PR's `pdep` form: 1623 vs 1681 µs on one thread, 112 vs 114 at 22 threads. Layer-weighted, adding #584 on top moves the numbers by under 1 % at nt = 1 and -1 % at nt = 2 / 4, which is within noise. That isn't worth a second routing rule, so I'm closing #584 in favour of this PR.
- IQ2_XXS is unchanged in all trees, as expected.

Thank you. Merged as one squashed commit under your name, rebased on v1.1.40, unchanged. The new rows are bit for bit ggml's on the AVX-512 and AVX2 paths, and a DeepSeek decode with the CPU lane gives the same tokens.

Released in **v1.1.41**: https://github.com/mw00/project-maya/releases/tag/v1.1.41
